claims.text: The substrate is Zircaloy-4 with a stated composition of Zr 98.2%, Sn 1.5%, Fe 0.2%, and Cr 0.1%.
The initial elemental Cr film is dense, defect-free, and amorphous.
Adding approximately 10 at.% Al to an elemental Cr coating will improve its durability on zirconium-alloy cladding.
The Al addition will form a protective composite oxide scale that limits Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
At approximately 10 at.% Al, oxidation will preferentially nucleate Al2O3.
Oxidation will cause outward Cr enrichment that stabilizes Cr2O3.
TiO2 will form if minor Ti is present.
The resulting oxide layer will be dense, continuous, and adherent.
The composite oxide will act as an effective oxygen barrier and reduce oxygen diffusion into the coating and substrate.
Reduced oxygen diffusion and suppressed Cr–Zr interdiffusion will maintain coating integrity and adhesion across normal-water and high-temperature-steam service regimes.
Al concentrations of at least 17 at.% cause intermetallic disruptions.
An intermediate Al concentration near 10 at.% is optimal.
Pure elemental Cr coatings initially provide strong protection to Zircaloy-4.
Pure Cr coatings can fail prematurely because of Cr–Zr interdiffusion, especially at elevated temperatures.
The 10 at.% Al-alloyed Cr coating will have a markedly lower oxidation rate than pure Cr.
The 10 at.% Al-alloyed Cr coating will exhibit less oxygen penetration than pure Cr.
The 10 at.% Al-alloyed Cr coating will retain better adhesion and coating integrity than pure Cr.
The 10 at.% Al-alloyed Cr coating will exhibit less Cr–Zr interdiffusion than pure Cr.
The proposed benefits apply at approximately 1000 °C for 60 minutes in flowing steam, potentially at 1100 °C for 30 minutes, and under subcritical-water conditions.
Analogous high-entropy-alloy studies provide prior grounds for expecting an intermediate Al addition to be beneficial.

contradictions.description: The specified substrate and intervention introduce no Ti, yet the mechanism describes formation of an Al2O3–TiO2–Cr2O3 composite as if TiO2 were part of the expected scale. The structural-mediator field only conditionally mentions TiO2 if Ti is present, leaving no identified Ti source in the stated system.
